--First came नाद from the Supreme Brahman, then ओङ्कार and then मन्त्रोपनिषद्। ब्रह्मा created अक्षरस्, and out of his four mouths appeared the four Vedas, which were taught to his sons. This was handed down by tradition through the ages.

Originally one, rearranged by व्यास into four सम्हितास्--ऋग्, Yajus, सामन् and Atharvan: distribution among his pupils done by कृष्णद्वैपायन with the help of Paila, Jaimini, Sumantu, and वैशम्पायन: growth of शाखास्. Lost in a deluge. Then Hari. taught them to ब्रह्मा who taught in his turn to his sons. A three fold division of the Vedas conveys the truth of Brahman and आत्मन्. In these Hari manifests himself: its metres are गायत्री, उष्णिक् and so on.
